Kai: heads up — noticed a p95 regression on canary after the kernel-selector tweak. Small-ish 512-token requests jumped ~+5ms p95 on host-side. Looks like tokenization + streaming framing (grpc/http2) spiking.

Infra-Bot: perf-alert: canary/host-runtime p95 above baseline (5.2ms). dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/canary/1750004567 :rotating_light:

Tess: can you paste the flame/profile? Is KV cache hit-rate affected or is this pure host I/O/tokenize? @Kai

Josh: quick sampling from a noisy run — attaching snippet:
```
# top 10 stacks (sample count)
grpc::Http2Stream::Read -> 38
host::tokenizer::Tokenize -> 32
syscall::read -> 28
syscall::writev -> 25
host::stream::frame_assemble -> 20
```
KV cache hitrate for the same window: 97% (no obvious eviction spike).

Anna: my guess: kernel selector change picked a variant with lower batch capacity for the common seq-lengths, so more single-request batches => more small writev/syscall overhead. Did the seq_len distribution change?

Kai: good call — after digging: median seq_len shifted from ~80 -> ~150 after the model micro-update. The kernel picker now prefers the fast-low-latency kernel that doesn't support aggressive batching for those lengths. So we lost batching density. Host tokenization work also increased slightly because tokenizer path changed for longer sequences.

Tess: two immediate mitigations: 1) force the previous kernel for the canary traffic (rollback selector) and 2) temporarily increase batch-window to 2ms for that kernel so we coalesce more. Also enable prefix KV caching for short responses to avoid re-tokenize in edge cases.

Kai: will try a canary rollback + batch-window bump. Planning to run the load probe again in ~15m and post new samples.

Josh: sgtm. If you need a quick script to flip kernel selector I can run it. :thumbsup:

Kai: thanks — will ping when new numbers are in.
